status: Three proposed source-backed state associations; no canonical profile or Site edits

associations.name: Cayuse
associations.associationType: Historical homeland described by the constituent tribal government
associations.period: Historical homeland before and during nineteenth-century territorial change
associations.sourceTitle: Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation — A Brief History of CTUIR
associations.evidenceNote: In its account of the lower Columbia peoples, CTUIR locates Cayuse communities along Blue Mountain tributary valleys and quotes a historical description placing most of their country in Oregon, with a smaller part in Washington Territory. This supports an Oregon historical connection; it does not confine Cayuse history to Oregon.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML text inspected: People of the lower Columbia, lines 94–100. Separate CTUIR About page, lines 61 and 73, identifies Cayuse as one of three constituent peoples and gives the shared government address at Pendleton, Oregon. Owner Umatilla study includes the history URL as a reading lead; original content was independently read for this map association.
limits: Cayuse, Umatilla and Walla Walla are distinct constituent peoples. The shared CTUIR government is not an interchangeable identity label.
The proposed record is a historical state connection, not an exclusive homeland boundary, current reservation polygon or current-law review.

associations.name: Clackamas
associations.associationType: Historical village and continuing ancestral-place connection
associations.period: Village history before the 1855 treaty and forced removal; later Grand Ronde account of ancestral connection
associations.sourceTitle: Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde — Vision for Willamette Falls Property
associations.evidenceNote: Grand Ronde places its Willamette Falls property on the east bank of the Willamette River in Oregon City. It identifies the former Kosh-huk-shix village there as a Clackamas community and describes treaty cession and forced removal to Grand Ronde. This directly supports an Oregon historical-place connection.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML text inspected: tumwata village | Oregon City, lines 54–58; continuing stewardship statement at line 72. Only the publicly named city/falls context is used. No coordinates or archaeological site geometry were copied.
limits: Grand Ronde is a confederated government with multiple constituent peoples; this record does not treat all Grand Ronde history as specifically Clackamas.
The path year and event dates within this page are not used to claim a current development-project status.
This is one public ancestral-place connection, not a complete Clackamas territory or a cadastral/rights boundary.

associations.name: Clatskanie
associations.associationType: Historical village-region connection in specialist scholarship
associations.period: Early nineteenth-century villages in the Portland Basin
associations.sourceTitle: Robert Boyd and Henry Zenk — Portland Basin Chinookan Villages in the early 1800s (Oregon Encyclopedia)
associations.evidenceNote: Boyd and Zenk explicitly place non-Chinookan Clatskanie villages in present-day Columbia County in the Portland Basin. The named county supplies the Oregon state connection. Their separate treatment of these communities avoids confusing Clatskanie with Chinookan villages or with Clatsop.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML introduction inspected, lines 25–40, especially line 34; the article identifies its authors and distinguishes the non-Chinookan communities from the principal Chinookan village table. Corroborating Boyd Wapato Valley entry, line 46, locates Clatskanies with an 1855 temporary reserve at Milton Creek near St. Helens. The linked St. Helens entry, lines 32–38, identifies that town as the Columbia County seat and situates it on the lower Columbia. State indexing resolves this explicitly named Oregon county; it is not inferred from the encyclopedia project title alone.
limits: This is historical settlement evidence, not a claim that the modern city of Clatskanie is itself a tribal government.
Clatskanie and Clatsop are distinct labels; no Clatsop source is reused for this record.
The sources inspected here do not establish an exclusive territory, present citizenship, contemporary political continuity or which modern government should speak for all Clatskanie descendants.

batchLimits: Only Cayuse, Clackamas and Clatskanie were reviewed. Each record supplies one useful connection, not comprehensive geographic coverage.
Map-content inspection does not promote a canonical profile to researched or adequate status.
Additional related passages were read only to resolve scope/geography; they are not counted as separate substantive profile sources.
